reporting-org.narrative: The Uganda Association of Women Lawyers ( FIDA Uganda)

title.narrative: We Cannot Wait Towards an Inclusive and Diverse Women's Movement in the GHoA

description.narrative:
With support from Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Netherlands), FIDA Uganda is implementing a five-year project, titled We Cannot Wait towards an Inclusive and diverse women Movement in the Greater Horn of Africa. This is a Consortium implementled project headed by SIHA. This project builds on the complementarity of project partners and years of shared experience and goals in the region, to strengthen the women’s movement, advocate for an inclusive and feminist legal framework and link together women’s organizations to push a gender-focused agenda in the region. The project’s long term strategic objective is “Women in the Greater Horn of Africa will be leading and defining the political, sociocultural and economic agenda through a gender lens at all levels.” The specific objectives of the project are; 1. Women’s rights activists and organizations (WRA/Os) are advocating for policy, law reform, and social norms. 2. WRA/Os in GHoA form an inclusive and diverse coalition with shared agendas. 3. WRA/Os engage actively and visibly in existing or new political and social platforms to promote their agendas.
In Uganda, the project is implemented in 4 districts of Gulu, Lira, Pader, and Kampala.

description.narrative: Laws blocked, adopted or improved to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere.

comment.narrative: Although the laws exist, some of them are vague and require ammendments including Succession Amendment Bill; the Land Amendment Bill; the Chattels Securities Act, No. 7 of 2014 to enable the use of personal property or chattels and not only land as security; the National Legal Aid Bill; and the Marriage and Divorce Bill; the National Transitional Justice Bill; The Minimum Wage

Push for an agenda on law reform especially pending Bills such as the Succession (Amendment) Bill, the Sexual Offences Bill, the Market bill, Employment (Sexual Harassment regulation 2012), and the repeal of the Anti-Pornography Act.

Enactment of the Employment (Amendment) act 2023: FIDA advocated for the enactment of the Employment (Amendment) Bill. FIDA-Uganda contributed to the consolidated version, redefining Labour Officers' powers and removing quasi-judicial functions. They prohibited discrimination against breastfeeding mothers, required lactation stations, and provided protections for pregnant women.
Succession Amendment Act 2022: In response to the unconstitutional provisions declared in 2007 for sex discrimination, FIDA-Uganda supported the merging of two bills into the Succession (Amendment) Bill, 2021, which was gazetted on September 27, 2021. FIDA-Uganda participated in various consultative meetings convened by the Law Reform Commission until the law was officially enacted in 2022.
FIDA-Uganda also seeks to challenge the various provisions of the law that continue to deny women their property rights despite its passage.
Sexual Offences Bill.
In partnership with Uganda Women Parliamentary Association (UWOPA) and Act Alliance, we met with six representatives from the Director of Public Prosecutions’ office to discuss key provisions of the Bill related to the prosecution of cases. Key discussions focused on the prosecution of offences such as: Clause 13: Defilement; Clause 14: Aggravated Defilement; Clause 23: Compensation; Clause 27: Corroboration of Evidence in Sexual Offences

title.narrative: Number of private sector company policies blocked, adopted or improved to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere.

description.narrative: Private sector company policies blocked, adopted or improved to promote women’s voice, agency, leadership, and representative participation in decision-making processes in public, private and civic sphere.

comment.narrative: FIDA will support the Safeguarding Policy in the Private Sector, the Works Compensation Act.
FIDA will support the Safeguarding Policy in the Private Sector, the Works Compensation Act.

Although FIDA had planned to influence the safeguarding policy and Workmans Compensation Act, these were not done and instead FIDA-Uganda successfully advocated for a ban on the practice of using National Identification cards as collateral for loans. The National Identification and Registration Bureau (NIRA) officially prohibited individuals from using their national ID cards as security for loans. This change was brought about by grassroots Women's Rights Advocates (WRAs) who participated in a social accountability forum organized by FIDA-Uganda. They urged the Uganda Microfinance Regulatory Authority (UMRA) to step in and put an end to this practice by money lenders.
FIDA will support the Safeguarding Policy in the Private Sector, the Works Compensation Act.

comment.narrative: None was planned since Uganda is already a signatory to CEDAW and also ratified the Maputo protocol
None was planned

Although not planned originally, FIDA Uganda contributed significantly to the ratification of the International Labour Convention 190 by Uganda in August 2023. They played a leading role in the Technical Working Group, engaging with Members of Parliament, civil society organizations, and the Minister for Gender, Labour, and Social Development to expedite the ratification process. Additionally, with support from the WCW project, FIDA Uganda facilitated the review and submission of Uganda's first State report on the implementation of the Maputo Protocol to the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights, highlighting Uganda's commitment to upholding women's rights and international obligations.

comment.narrative: Revise of the GBV ordinance food security ordinance, and and alcohol control bill
Review the GBV ordinance and Food security ordinance, alcohol control bill

FIDA Uganda has been active at the local government level, participating in the review of the Gender-Based Violence (GBV) ordinance and the Persons with Disabilities ordinance. These efforts aimed to improve local by-laws to better promote women's rights and inclusion.
However, 3 ordinances in Pader; The Alcohol Control Ordinance, GBV Ordinance and the food Security Ordinance await the attorney general's certification.
In 2021, FIDA focused on establishing coalitions and strengthening their capacity for legal and legal reform.
FIDA will continue to influence the GBV ordinance, food security ordinance, and alcohol control bill.

title.narrative: Number of individuals (female) with strengthened capacity (knowledge and skills) to advance women's rights and gender equality (age non-specified)

description.narrative: Female individuals have strengthened capacity (knowledge and skills) to advance women's rights and gender equality

comment.narrative: The baseline quantitative values are zero at this point as this indicator defines an increase. Summary of Baseline findings: Most of the activists are freelance and engage on issues supported by various organizations. Current leadership status among the participants varied across the countries; Regionally 55(50%), South Sudan 13(93%), Sudan 17(68%), Somaliland 4(57%), Uganda 16 (34%), Somali 2(20%) and Ethiopia 3(38%). Most of these leadership positions are held at the community level. Additionally, at WROs level, the average number of female staff across the countries is 167.5 while that of the male is staff is 23.3. Several women have risen to leadership positions across the surveyed countries. Somaliland had the highest number of women in leadership positions at 34%. This was followed by Ethiopia with 32%. The remaining countries, South Sudan, Sudan Uganda and Somali, had a mean of less than 10% The perception of participants in political affairs was also assessed. Although not very positive across the region except for Uganda, almost half of the participants 39(35%) perceive that the political process is fair for women aspirants; Uganda 27(57.4%), Ethiopia 7(87.5%) while only Somali 1(10%), South Sudan 1(7.1%), and Sudan 1(4.0%) and Somaliland 2(8.6%). Structural conditions limiting women’s participation in decision-making roles include high levels of illiteracy; low levels of education, awareness of women’s rights, and self-esteem; lack of energy/time outside of economic activities; and high rates of VAW/G. Some women face more barriers than others: women from minority clans; internally displaced women and other migrants living in camps and informal urban settlements; poor rural pastoral women; women with disabilities; young women.
FIDA Uganda targeted 315 WRAs over this period

From the midterm review conducted in June 2023, out of the 315 WRAs supported by the project under the Uganda Women’s Coalition, 199(62%) of them reported having strengthened advocacy and lobbying skills. This is seen from the number of noteworthy initiatives that demonstrate how much WRAs' advocacy and lobbying abilities have improved. For instance, the WRAs in Pader, Uganda, were successful in their lobbying efforts to repurpose funds meant for fencing at a health center to renovate a maternity ward, which was in dire need of repair. Their improved abilities also made it possible for female council members to bring up issues in the local tongue without alerting the speaker beforehand, which strengthened support for women's causes inside the council. Male stakeholders have endorsed this, seeing how crucial it is to work together to execute and support WRA initiatives to remain up to date on community needs. Notwithstanding obstacles including a dearth of funding for campaigns and patriarchal customs, the WRAs have had success directly engaging influential people like the speaker of parliament. In Gulu, Lira, Pader, and Kampala, WRAs have also participated in policy advocacy, movement building, and economic empowerment. They have also coordinated via online platforms and carried out community outreach, underscoring their enhanced advocacy efforts.
In 2021, the focus will be on mapping and identifying WRAs and Os to participate in the project, establishing coalitions, and engaging in capacity-building activities for the WRAs and Os.

We have received feedback from various men in leadership positions (especially the ones we have closely engaged) on their improved attitude and changes in their practices towards women's issues. The following details describe the nature of the improved attitudes we have registered. The Mayor Lira City gave women an opportunity to apply for jobs in the city, and the Lira city speaker- allowed women to speak in their local languages during the council meetings. Acholi prime minister made commitment to call culture leaders and indulged them on the rights of women to women land. Also, the RDC of pader--held a joint operation with police and army to protect women when heading back to their homes after late working hours of the evening market, Mayor Nakawa division, MP -Nakawa, RCC -Nakawa have also supported on issues faced by market women in Nakawa.
